observation_summary: The SerializationUtils.clone method fails with a ClassNotFoundException when attempting to clone primitive types (e.g., int.class).
hypothesis: The ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream.resolveClass method fails to correctly resolve primitive class names because it lacks a lookup mechanism for primitive types, which are not found via standard Class.forName calls.
prediction: The code will be updated to include a mapping of primitive type names to their corresponding Class objects and a logic branch in resolveClass to check this map when Class.forName fails.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the addition of a primitiveTypes map and logic to query this map within the resolveClass method, confirming that the procedural logic for resolving classes was incomplete for primitive types.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic failure in the class resolution procedure. The method was missing the logic to handle primitive types, which are special cases in Java serialization. This is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization), but a flaw in the computational strategy used to resolve class names. It is not a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object) because the functionality (cloning) exists and works for non-primitive objects; it just needed a procedural update to handle a specific subset of inputs.
evidence_used: The bug report states that SerializationUtils throws ClassNotFoundException when cloning primitive classes.
The fix diff shows the addition of a primitiveTypes map and a lookup mechanism in resolveClass.
The stack trace shows the failure occurs during class resolution in ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check (if cls != null), the root cause is the absence of the primitive type resolution logic itself, which is a procedural/algorithmic deficiency.
The capability to clone objects is already present; this is a local procedural correction to handle primitive types, not a missing design-level feature.
